name: CarePulse
lede: Outpatient system for Indian clinics covering registration, live queue, vitals, consultation, lab orders and results, prescriptions and pharmacy dispensing for 6 staff roles.

points.label: Backend
points.text: **185 REST API operations** in Python / FastAPI across 36 feature modules, each built as router, service and repository layers with SQLAlchemy 2.0 and Alembic migrations.

points.label: Data & multi-tenancy
points.text: **PostgreSQL row-level security** per tenant plus a role-permission matrix; clinical writes go to an **append-only ledger** (trigger-enforced) enabling “as-of” replay.

points.label: Concurrency & jobs
points.text: Queue tokens stay unique under simultaneous sign-ups using a lock plus **bounded retry**; a background job is **safe to rerun** and to run on several workers via PostgreSQL advisory locks.

points.label: Correctness
points.text: A Playwright test exposed commits running **after the response was sent** (stale reads); fixed so every 2xx means the write is committed, with a test checking every route.

points.label: Testing
points.text: **925 pytest tests** (336 unit, 300 integration on real PostgreSQL, 289 security) plus Hypothesis and Playwright; a latency test asserts **p95 search < 300 ms over 50,000 patients**.

points.label: Security
points.text: JWT with refresh tokens, **argon2** password hashing, sign-in rate limiting with Retry-After, and an **audit trail of every patient-data read**.

points.label: CI/CD
points.text: **GitHub Actions** starts a throwaway PostgreSQL per job and runs pytest, ruff, strict mypy, ESLint, dependency audits and Docker builds.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body:
Outpatient clinics run on a daily patient queue. One visit moves through registration, the live queue, vitals, consultation, lab orders and results, prescriptions and pharmacy dispensing, and each step belongs to a different person: receptionist, nurse, doctor, lab technician, pharmacist. With the clinic administrator, that makes six staff roles, and CarePulse gives each one its own workflow on one shared patient record, for several clinics at once.

Three things make that harder than a typical CRUD app:

- **Concurrency.** Two receptionists registering patients at the same moment must never get the same queue token.
- **Isolation.** Clinics share one database, and one clinic must never see another clinic's patients.
- **Trust.** Clinical records can't be quietly overwritten, and every read of patient data has to be accountable.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.body:
CarePulse is built by a team of two: a Python backend on FastAPI and PostgreSQL, and a React and TypeScript front end.

Tests have been in the repository since its first commit rather than added at the end. The goal was simple: if the suite passes, a clinic's day actually works, including the parts that only break under concurrent use.

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.body:
The API has **185 operations across 36 feature modules**, and every module is split the same way, so each new feature has an obvious home:

- **Router**: the HTTP layer.
- **Service**: the business rules.
- **Repository**: data access through SQLAlchemy 2.0, with schema changes as Alembic migrations.

PostgreSQL does more than store rows. It enforces tenant isolation, keeps clinical history append-only, and coordinates background work.

sections.heading: Technical decisions
sections.body:
### Isolate tenants in the database, not only in code

Access is checked twice: by a role-permission matrix in the application, and again by **PostgreSQL row-level security** per tenant. If application code ever forgets a filter, the database still returns only the current clinic's rows.

### Make clinical history append-only

Clinical writes go to an **append-only ledger**, enforced by database triggers rather than by convention. Nothing is overwritten, which makes it possible to replay a record as it stood at any point in time.

### Handle concurrency where it happens

Queue tokens are issued under a lock with a **bounded retry**, so simultaneous sign-ups stay unique. The background job that updates overdue follow-ups takes a **PostgreSQL advisory lock**, so it is safe to rerun and safe to run on more than one worker.

### Security basics, done completely

JWT with refresh tokens, **argon2** password hashing, sign-in rate limiting that answers with Retry-After, and an **audit trail of every read of patient data**.

sections.heading: Challenges
sections.body:
### The commit that happened after the response

A Playwright end-to-end run exposed a subtle bug: the database commit was running **after the HTTP response had been sent**. A client that refetched straight away could read stale data. The fix guarantees that every 2xx response means the write is committed, and a test now checks that for **every route**, so a new endpoint can't bring the bug back.

### Proving search stays fast

Patient search has to stay quick as a clinic's records grow. Instead of assuming it would, a latency test asserts that **95% of searches finish in under 300 ms with 50,000 patients**.

sections.heading: Trade-offs
sections.body:
- **Row-level security fails quietly.** A missing policy shows up as "no rows", not as an error, which is why dedicated security tests matter as much as the policies themselves.
- **Full history costs storage.** An append-only ledger keeps every change, so it grows faster than a table that is updated in place, and reading the current state takes more work.
- **A bounded retry can run out.** Under extreme contention a registration can fail after its retries; the design prefers a clear error to a duplicate queue token.
- **Real databases make tests slower.** Integration tests run against a real PostgreSQL, and CI starts a throwaway database per job. Slower runs are the price of testing what production actually does.

sections.heading: Results
sections.body:
- **185 REST API operations** across 36 feature modules, covering six staff roles. An operation is one method and path in the OpenAPI spec.
- **925 pytest tests**, counted as pytest collects them: 336 unit, 300 integration on real PostgreSQL and 289 security, plus Hypothesis property tests and Playwright end-to-end runs.
- **p95 patient search under 300 ms** with 50,000 patients, asserted by a test.
- Every push runs pytest, ruff, strict mypy, ESLint, dependency audits and Docker builds in **GitHub Actions**.

CarePulse is still in progress, so these figures are a snapshot from October 2026. The repository is private.

sections.heading: Lessons learned
sections.body:
- People trust internal tools because of **permissions, audit trails and reliability**, not only features.
- Testing is how I find out whether a design really works. A subtle bug here was found by a Playwright run, not by reading the code.
- Look for where a system breaks rather than where it works. It's a habit from evaluating LLM responses at Ethara AI, and it applies to APIs just as well.

name: HireStream
tagline: Job portal for recruiters and candidates
lede: A full-stack job portal with REST APIs for users, companies, jobs and applications, covering recruiter and candidate workflows.

points.label: Backend & APIs
points.text: Built **15+ REST endpoints** (Node.js, Express) for users, companies, jobs and applications, with **JWT auth middleware** guarding protected routes.

points.label: Data modeling
points.text: Designed **MongoDB schemas** (Mongoose) for 4 collections linked by ObjectId references; used **nested population** to return applicants with profiles and applications with company details in one request.

points.label: Hiring workflow
points.text: Duplicate-application checks, a **pending / accepted / rejected** status pipeline for recruiters, and case-insensitive **$regex keyword search** over job titles and descriptions.

points.label: Security & uploads
points.text: **JWT in httpOnly cookies**, bcrypt hashing and recruiter-only routes; photos, résumés and company logos uploaded via **Multer + Cloudinary**.

name: TerraLoom
lede: A property listing platform with listing CRUD, reviews and owner-only edit and delete permissions.

points.label: Authorization
points.text: Owner-only listing edits and author-only review deletion via Express middleware; **cascade-deletes reviews** with a Mongoose post-delete hook.

points.label: Auth & security
points.text: Passport.js sessions **stored in MongoDB** (connect-mongo), **Joi** schema validation and **Helmet** CSP headers.

points.label: Maps & media
points.text: **Mapbox** geocoding saved as **GeoJSON**; listing images uploaded to Cloudinary via Multer.
